newsitem.title: CANADA: Busang discoverer to give up Canadian mining award.
newsitem.headline: Busang discoverer to give up Canadian mining award.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd's former exploration chief, John Felderhof, will surrender a prestigious award given to him last year by a Canadian mining association, the group said on Thursday.
Felderhof was given the Prospector of the Year award last year by the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada for his work in finding the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
Busang, once touted by Felderhof and Bre-X as the richest gold find of the century, was found to be a massive fraud earlier this month.
Bre-X's stock collapsed, its shares were delisted from Canadian exchanges and Nasdaq and at least 10 lawsuits have been filed against the company.

"In light of the present circumstances and uncertainty around the existence of the deposit as originally described, Mr. Felderhof has agreed to voluntarily surrender his award," the Prospectors association said in a statement on Thursday.
Felderhof was fired by Bre-X earlier this month. He has denied any wrongdoing and now lives in virtual seclusion on his US$2.9 million estate in the Cayman Islands.
Meanwhile, another class action lawsuit over the Bre-X scandal at was filed Thursday in British Columbia.

The lawsuit names the Toronto Stock Exchange and brokerage Nesbitt Burns Inc., a subsidiary of the Bank of Montreal, as co-defendants along with Bre-X, its officers and directors, lawyer David Klein said.
Bre-X faces at least nine similar lawsuits in the United States and elsewhere in Canada. Nesbitt Burns has already been named in another Canadian case.
"We are working with lawyers from across Canada and in the United States in a coordinated effort to recover compensation for shareholders of Bre-X," Klein said.

"This is a case in which everyone from Bre-X Minerals, its directors and officers to brokers and regulators appear to have been so caught up in gold fever that they lost sight of their responsibilities to investors."
Klein filed the suit on behalf of Bill and Anne Williams, a carpenter and school secretary from Surrey, British Columbia, who invested C$53,000 in Bre-X shares.

The Supreme Court of British Columbia will rule whether to certify the suit as a class action on behalf of Bre-X shareholders in the province with a sub-class for shareholders outside British Columbia.
